channel.description: A doctor's daily pick of Korean healthcare news, summarized in English with links to the originals.

item.title: Tue, Nov 24 · A day of turf fights at the National Assembly
item.description: X-rays for Korean-medicine doctors, off-site work for medical technicians, cross-hiring of pharmacists: three bills on the same day, all about who may do what.
item.content:encoded:
Today in one line X-rays for Korean-medicine doctors, off-site work for medical technicians, cross-hiring of pharmacists: three bills on the same day, all about who may do what.

  1. Bill on X-rays for Korean-medicine doctors goes to subcommittee as both sides rally
    The welfare committee's subcommittee reviewed a medical law amendment on Nov 24 that would make any clinic founder the safety officer for diagnostic X-ray equipment. The Korean Medical Association rallied outside the Assembly calling it a back door for X-rays in Korean-medicine clinics; the Korean-medicine association held its own event urging passage.
    Source: Bosa, MTN
  2. Nurses back the X-ray bill; Seoul physicians demand an apology
    The Korea Nurses Association backed the amendment, citing patient choice and the burden of moving between clinics. The Seoul Medical Association said on Nov 24 that the nurses' group was undermining the licensing system and demanded an apology.
    Source: Bosa
  3. Medical technician bill clears subcommittee, allowing off-site work with a prescription
    The subcommittee passed an amendment to the medical technicians act on Nov 24, based on a compromise among professional groups. Technicians are defined as working 'under a doctor's direction', and off-site work is allowed on a doctor's prescription where other laws provide for it, with doctors confirming it through digital means.
    Source: Bosa
  4. Government urges caution on bill banning pharmacist–herbal pharmacist cross-hiring
    The health ministry said a pharmacy bill barring pharmacy owners from hiring the other license type could overly restrict freedom of occupation, and urged caution. The bill was expected to struggle at the Nov 24 subcommittee.
    Source: Dailypharm
  5. NHIS investigator bill stalls again on Nov 18
    After deferring a vote on Nov 16, the Legislation Committee again failed to act on Nov 18 as opposition members stayed away. The NHIS says the powers would cut investigations from 11 months to three and save about KRW 200bn a year; the justice ministry says conflict-of-interest concerns remain.
    Source: Seoul Economic Daily, Dailymedi
  6. Co-pay for rare and severe intractable diseases falls to 7% on Dec 1
    About 1.36 million registered patients with rare or severe intractable diseases will pay 7% instead of 10% for care from Dec 1. Average annual out-of-pocket costs are expected to fall from about KRW 750,000 to KRW 530,000, with a further cut to 5% in the first half of 2028.
    Source: Korea.kr
  7. Barofarm buys insolvent Jungwoo Pharm for KRW 10bn
    Barofarm, a pharmacy ordering platform that listed on KOSDAQ this month, was picked as the final buyer of Jungwoo Pharm, which is in court receivership. It will pay about KRW 10bn for 100% and gain an Asan plant and about 90 products.
    Source: Dailypharm
  8. In the US, prescriptions can now be written and sent inside ChatGPT
    US prescribing platform Photon launched a ChatGPT plug-in. Eligible US clinicians can review treatment options, then write and send prescriptions in the same chat, with interaction checks and pharmacy price comparisons.
    Source: Medigate News
  9. Drug safety chief inspects parametric release for IV fluids
    MFDS chief Oh Yu-kyoung visited HK inno.N's Osong plant on Nov 24 to review release based on process parameters instead of end-product sterility tests, and met three IV fluid makers. Stricter GMP had raised sterility test samples from one to ten or more.
    Source: Dailypharm

Source: Dr. Jordan, mednomics.co.kr

item.title: Mon, Nov 16 · Investigator bill pushed to the 18th, lab testing heads to court
item.description: All eyes are on the Legislation Committee meeting on the 18th. Whether the bill passes matters as much as how narrowly the law defines the investigators' scope.
item.content:encoded:
Today in one line All eyes are on the Legislation Committee meeting on the 18th. Whether the bill passes matters as much as how narrowly the law defines the investigators' scope.

  1. NHIS special investigator bill held at the Legislation Committee; vote expected on the 18th
    The committee took up the bill on Nov 16 but did not vote, choosing to review it with other bills amending the same law. Members asked how investigations would start and raised due-process concerns about adding criminal powers to existing audit powers.
    Source: Bosa, Khanews, Dailypharm
  2. Doctors rally at the Assembly; NHIS offers to limit scope to illegally opened clinics
    The Korean Medical Association rallied outside the Assembly on Nov 16 demanding the bill be withdrawn. The NHIS said it would limit investigations to non-doctor-owned clinics and rented-license pharmacies, not ordinary care or billing, and proposed an external review board.
    Source: Dailypharm, Nurse News
  3. Hypertension society threatens legal action over lab-testing fee overhaul
    At its autumn meeting in Gwangju on Nov 15, the society warned that cuts to lab-testing fees would hurt internal medicine clinics treating chronic disease. It threatened legal action against the notice and also opposed the NHIS investigator plan.
    Source: Bosa
  4. AI scribe Neardoc reaches 500 hospitals in five months
    The AI scribe drafts a SOAP note from the consultation in about five seconds. It says it has reached 500 hospitals and 970,000 records in five months, deletes raw audio immediately and checks each sentence against the conversation.
    Source: Bosa
  5. Three Chinese cancer drugs: Europe says yes, the US says no
    Europe's CHMP recommended approval of lung cancer drugs aumolertinib and sintilimab, while the US FDA did not approve ivonescimab. Regulators split on drugs from the same country.
    Source: Bosa
  6. Oral combination shows promise in endometrial cancer after immunotherapy
    In an early trial across 12 sites in Korea, the US and Japan, E7386 plus lenvatinib shrank tumors by the set threshold in 36.7% of patients and controlled disease in 70%. Among patients new to lenvatinib, 57.1% saw tumors shrink.
    Source: Bosa
  7. KDDW 2026 in Seoul, Nov 19–21, with 2,000 attendees from 30 countries
    Eight gastroenterology societies will present 456 studies. Updated Korean guidelines for MASLD and inflammatory bowel disease are due.
    Source: Bosa
  8. MFDS holds Innovative Medical Device Policy Forum 2026
    The drug safety ministry hosted a forum on Nov 16 for companies with or seeking innovative device status, joined by HIRA, on faster market entry.
    Source: Bosa

Source: Dr. Jordan, mednomics.co.kr
